title: Metered surge lanes, burst windows, and invoice notification flow for temporary capacity
creator: Maya Torres
description:
Problem: Customers on Dedicated want predictable throughput guarantees but occasionally need predictable short-term bursts. Today we offer 'surge pools' and ad-hoc temporary boosts, but billing and throttling behavior during bursts is confusing: customers see abrupt overage spikes, engineering gets paging noise, and product teams get support tickets asking for clearer notifications and opt-in settings.

Goal: Implement a metered surge-lane system and 'burst window' semantics that: (1) allow explicit short-lived capacity boosts that are separable from baseline committed capacity, (2) meter and present overage in a way that is predictable to customers (pro-rated, smoothed, with clear invoice line items), (3) provide operator controls to cap aggregate fleet exposure and trigger automatic throttles/fallbacks when risk thresholds are met, and (4) add user-facing notifications and billing events so admins can opt into or deny bursts.

Scope: Design and implement runtime allocator changes, billing event model, console UI hooks for burst policies, and telemetry/alerts. Do not include on-prem private installer changes in this ticket (follow-up).

Success criteria / Acceptance criteria:
- API for requesting a temporary boost (duration, max qps/slots) that returns an approved meter id and estimated cost impact.
- Runtime alloc honors burst lanes with weighted queueing so baseline SLOs degrade gracefully rather than fail-fast.
- Billing emits a separate 'burst_charge' line per meter id with pro-rated cost and a smoothing window option (1, 6, 24h) to distribute invoice impact.
- Admin console has a toggle to auto-approve up to X% of committed capacity as bursts and an explicit deny list for customers.
- On-call runbook updated to include new paging thresholds and hazard mitigation (auto-fallbacking to secondary model variants).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Metered vs. free bursts: We chose metered bursts to align incentives and reduce surprise billing. Free grace credits were considered but complicate accounting and can be gamed.
- Smoothing window: Smoothing reduces invoice spikes for customers but can defer accurate cost signals; default to 6h with opt-out.
- Enforcement model: Two options evaluated: pre-reserved surge pool (capacity set aside) vs. opportunistic surge lanes (best-effort weighted queues). We will implement opportunistic surge lanes with operator caps first (less waste), and evaluate pre-reserved lanes for high-tier customers in a follow-up.
- Throttling policy: When overall fleet exposure crosses threshold T1 (operator-set), start throttling new burst approvals; at T2 start conservative runtime preemption of low-priority bursts. This is easier to operate than per-customer hard limits but requires robust telemetry.

Telemetry & observability requirements:
- New metrics: burst.requests, burst.approved, burst.denied_reason, burst.charge_by_meter_id, fleet.burst_exposure_pct, runtime.preempted_bursts_count.
- Dashboards: per-customer burst usage, estimated vs actual cost delta, fleet exposure heatmap.
- Alerts: burst.exposure > 60% for 10m (warning), > 80% for 2m (page).

APIs and data model:
- POST /v1/dedicated/bursts request body: {customer_id, requested_qps, duration_minutes, smoothing_window_hours (optional)} -> returns {meter_id, approved_qps, estimated_cost_cents}. (See spec in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/docs/dedicated-burst-spec)
- Billing events: emit structured event to billing pipeline: type=burst_charge, meter_id, customer_id, window_start, window_end, units_consumed, unit_price_cents, smoothing_window. (Billing team API PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/213)

Operator controls and safety knobs:
- Fleet caps: global_max_burst_pct and per-cluster_max_burst_pct.
- Emergency kill switch: disable-burst-approvals endpoint for incidents.
- Auto-fallback policies: map to cheaper model variants when baseline latency or token cost budget breaches.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design: finalize API shape, billing event contract, and runtime queue weighting algorithm (this ticket).
2) Runtime prototype: implement opportunistic weighted queueing + per-request meter_id propagation (ENG spike pod).
3) Billing: wire burst_charge event into billing pipeline + smoothing logic (billing team).
4) Console: add admin toggles and per-customer burst page.
5) Telemetry & Alerting: dashboards and paging config.
6) Beta: roll out to a small subset of Dedicated customers with explicit opt-in.

Dependencies:
- Billing: pipeline changes to accept burst_charge events (depends on BUG-128 in billing backlog).
- Console: UI for admin controls (PM/Design story PM-4123 / DES-210).
- Runtime: queueing library change in serving runtime (ENG-20090).

Risks & mitigation:
- Surprise invoices: mitigate by sending 24h pre-burst estimation emails and real-time billing preview in console.
- Fleet instability from unbounded bursts: operator caps and gradual rollout with canary on 2 clusters.
- Abuse by customers scripting bursts: require burst API to be an authenticated admin-only action and rate-limited per account.

Rollout plan:
- Stage 1 (two weeks): internal feature flag + telemetry in staging clusters.
- Stage 2 (one month): limited beta with 12 customers, billing in preview mode (no real charges) and in-console estimates.
- Stage 3 (after beta): enable metered billing for opt-in customers and gradually open auto-approve based on credit score/contract.

Open questions:
- Default unit price for burst capacity vs committed capacity (pricing to be set by finance).
- Whether smoothing windows should be configurable per-customer or per-meter. Recommend per-meter now.
